title: "You're on a bicycle with a little motor": Benefits and Challenges of Using AI Code Assistants
measured_outcome_verified: Developer experiences, perceived benefits, challenges, and coping strategies when using AI code assistants.
measurement_unit_verified: Qualitative interview evidence.
supporting_evidence: The study is based on interviews with 14 software developers about daily experiences using AI code assistants.
verification_notes: No observed productivity/effort outcome with an identifiable workflow boundary.

title: A Large-Scale Survey on the Usability of AI Programming Assistants: Successes and Challenges
measured_outcome_verified: Developer-reported usability, motivations, successful use cases, and challenges with AI programming assistants.
measurement_unit_verified: Survey responses from 410 developers.
supporting_evidence: Claims about finishing tasks quickly and reducing keystrokes are reported motivations rather than directly observed task-time outcomes.
verification_notes: Perceived usability/productivity is insufficient for workflow-boundary coding.

title: AI-Assisted Code Authoring at Scale: Fine-Tuning, Deploying, and Mixed Methods Evaluation
measured_outcome_verified: Observed use and contribution of the CodeCompose code-authoring system.
measurement_unit_verified: Hidden-line reproduction accuracy, share of authored code coming directly from CodeCompose, usage/adoption metrics, and feedback.
supporting_evidence: CodeCompose was deployed to thousands of developers; the paper reports that a measurable share of authored code comes directly from the assistant and evaluates suggestion-generation accuracy.
verification_notes: B1 because the measured behavioral output concerns local code authoring/suggestion use rather than completion of an end-to-end task.

title: AI-Tutoring in Software Engineering Education
measured_outcome_verified: Student interaction patterns and experiences with an LLM-based AI tutor.
measurement_unit_verified: Tutor interaction data and exploratory survey responses.
supporting_evidence: The study identifies student user types from interactions with the AI tutor and examines perceived advantages and challenges.
verification_notes: No concrete productivity/effort outcome with an identifiable software-development workflow boundary.

title: Accelerating Software Development Using Generative AI: ChatGPT Case Study
procedure: Case study, Concept Implementation (Proof of Concept)
pilot_outcome: SDLC case study measuring person-day effort across requirements, design, source code, and test-case work; effort explicitly includes ChatGPT response review and correction time.
measured_outcome_verified: Total software-development effort across requirements, design, source-code, and test-case generation; effort includes review and correction of ChatGPT outputs.
measurement_unit_verified: Person-days
supporting_evidence: The study reports ~22 person-days for the overall SDLC process and states that the effort includes ChatGPT response review time and correction time.
evidence_page_or_section: Table 6 / effort analysis; immediately before Threats to Validity
verification_notes: B3 retained because review/correction are explicitly included in measured effort; no verified merge/deployment outcome.

title: An Analysis of the Costs and Benefits of Autocomplete in IDEs
pilot_outcome: Programming tasks; documentation time; keystrokes; post-study API knowledge
measured_outcome_verified: Developer productivity while completing programming tasks with or without IDE autocomplete.
measurement_unit_verified: Number of tasks completed; per-task development time; documentation-reading time; coding time; keystrokes.
supporting_evidence: The study defines productivity using the number of tasks completed and time spent finishing each individual task, and reconstructs per-task development time from screen recordings.
verification_notes: B2 retained because the productivity outcome ends at completion of the programming task. Local interaction measures are also reported but no downstream review/integration stage is included.

title: An Industry Case Study on Adoption of AI-based Programming Assistants
measured_outcome_verified: Practitioner adoption, usage patterns, motivations, and perceived benefits/challenges of AI programming assistants.
measurement_unit_verified: Online survey responses from 72 employees.
supporting_evidence: The study asks how practitioners perceive and use AI tools; reported acceleration of searching, typing, and syntax recall is survey-based rather than an observed effort outcome.
verification_notes: No objectively bounded productivity/effort outcome.

title: Ansible Lightspeed: A Code Generation Service for IT Automation
measured_outcome_verified: Utility and usage of the Ansible Lightspeed code-generation service.
measurement_unit_verified: User acceptance, rejected suggestions, utilization, retention, and sentiment indicators.
supporting_evidence: The evaluation focuses on user acceptance, retention, rejected suggestions, and sentiments among real users.
verification_notes: Usage/adoption telemetry does not establish a productivity or effort boundary under the current coding protocol.

title: Better Together? An Evaluation of AI-Supported Code Translation
procedure: Case Study, Controlled experiment within-subjects, Survey
measured_outcome_verified: Performance and work process when translating Java data structures into Python with and without AI-generated translations.
measurement_unit_verified: Translation errors/quality, task process measures, subjective workload, and completion within a 30-minute task window.
supporting_evidence: Thirty-two software engineers performed Java-to-Python translation tasks with and without model-generated translations. The measured outcome is the produced translation and its quality/error profile.
verification_notes: B2 retained conservatively. Test code exists in the study materials, but available evidence does not establish testing as a separately measured participant verification stage.

title: Beyond Code Generation: An Observational Study of ChatGPT Usage in Software Engineering Practice
measured_outcome_verified: ChatGPT usage purposes, dialogue characteristics, perceived usefulness, and trust in industrial software-engineering practice.
measurement_unit_verified: Qualitative analysis of ChatGPT dialogues and exit-survey responses.
supporting_evidence: Twenty-four professionals used ChatGPT for one week; the study qualitatively analyzes their dialogues and reported experience rather than bounded effort.
verification_notes: Observed usage is empirical, but no productivity/effort measure permits a B1-B4 boundary assignment.

title: Developer Experiences with a Contextualized AI Coding Assistant: Usability, Expectations, and Outcomes
measured_outcome_verified: Usability, expectations, perceived time savings, and experiences with a contextualized coding assistant.
measurement_unit_verified: Controlled-session observations and participant-reported outcomes.
supporting_evidence: The source reports that, according to participants, the assistant resulted in time savings and easier documentation access.
verification_notes: Time savings are participant-reported rather than an objectively bounded task-effort measure.

title: Generation Probabilities Are Not Enough: Uncertainty Highlighting in AI Code Completions
measured_outcome_verified: Task completion performance when programmers edit AI-generated code completions under different uncertainty-highlighting conditions.
measurement_unit_verified: Task completion time, targeted edits, and task/code accuracy.
supporting_evidence: Thirty programmers complete code-editing tasks; highlighting tokens likely to be edited leads to faster task completion and more targeted edits.
verification_notes: B2 because the measured outcome ends at completion/correction of the programming task; no downstream review or delivery stage.

title: How ChatGPT shapes the future labour market situation of software engineers: A Finnish Delphi study
measured_outcome_verified: Expert expectations regarding the future labour-market impact of ChatGPT on software engineers.
measurement_unit_verified: Delphi judgments/interviews.
supporting_evidence: The study forecasts changes in software-engineering work and labour markets rather than measuring developer workflow effort.
verification_notes: Prospective expert judgment is outside the empirical boundary analysis.

title: How Far Are We? The Triumphs and Trials of Generative AI in Learning Software Engineering
measured_outcome_verified: Student productivity while performing software-engineering tasks with ChatGPT versus traditional resources.
measurement_unit_verified: Task-based productivity/performance measures plus self-efficacy and frustration.
supporting_evidence: A between-subjects study with 22 participants evaluates ChatGPT while students perform software-engineering tasks and reports the productivity comparison between conditions.
verification_notes: B2 retained because the observable productivity construct concerns completion/performance of the assigned SE task.

title: In-IDE Code Generation from Natural Language: Promise and Challenges
procedure: Controlled Experiment, Survey, Concept implementation (Proof of concept)
pilot_outcome: Fourteen Python programming tasks; productivity, quality, and correctness
measured_outcome_verified: Developer productivity, correctness, and code characteristics while completing Python programming tasks with or without an NL-to-code IDE plugin.
measurement_unit_verified: Task completion time, correctness score, SLOC, and cyclomatic complexity.
supporting_evidence: Developers completed 14 Python programming tasks. The quantitative models use task completion time and correctness as principal task-performance outcomes.
evidence_page_or_section: Human Study Design; RQ1; task-performance regression tables
verification_notes: B2 retained because the measured workflow boundary is completion of the programming task, not review, integration, or delivery.

title: Navigating the Complexity of Generative AI Adoption in Software Engineering—RCR Report
measured_outcome_verified: Factors affecting GenAI adoption and integration into software-engineering workflows.
measurement_unit_verified: Survey constructs and PLS-SEM relationships in an adoption framework.
supporting_evidence: The RCR report concerns adoption factors, perceived usefulness, compatibility, social influences, and organizational factors.
verification_notes: No measured productivity/effort outcome with an identifiable boundary.

title: Performance, Workload, Emotion, and Self-Efficacy of Novice Programmers Using AI Code Generation
pilot_outcome: Programming performance and efficiency under time pressure
measured_outcome_verified: Programming performance and efficiency of novice programmers coding with and without GitHub Copilot under time pressure.
measurement_unit_verified: Programming performance/efficiency plus workload, emotion, and self-efficacy measures.
supporting_evidence: A within-subject study with seventeen novice programmers compares coding performance with and without GitHub Copilot under time pressure and reports changes in programming efficiency.
verification_notes: B2 retained because the empirical efficiency outcome concerns completion/performance of programming work; no downstream review or delivery stage is included in the available evidence.

title: Productivity assessment of neural code completion
pilot_outcome: Suggestion acceptance and persistence; code-completion interaction telemetry
measured_outcome_verified: Observable GitHub Copilot interaction metrics used as proxies for perceived developer productivity.
measurement_unit_verified: Suggestion acceptance rate, completion persistence, accepted characters per active hour, accepted completions per active hour, and related interaction-normalized metrics.
supporting_evidence: The study relates developers' perceived productivity to directly measurable code-completion telemetry. Acceptance rate is the strongest observed correlate, while persistence and other local completion metrics are also analyzed.
verification_notes: B1 retained because the empirical productivity evidence concerns local code-completion interactions rather than completed tasks or downstream workflow stages.

title: Reading Between the Lines: Modeling User Behavior and Costs in AI-Assisted Programming
pilot_outcome: Coding tasks and time costs of Copilot interaction activities
measured_outcome_verified: Time costs and behavioral states associated with programmer interaction with GitHub Copilot.
measurement_unit_verified: Annotated interaction segments, state dwell time, transitions, and time attributable to code-recommendation interaction.
supporting_evidence: Twenty-one programmers completed coding tasks and retrospectively annotated their sessions using CUPS. The analysis measures how programmers spend time across AI-interaction states and estimates the time cost attributable to recommendation-system interaction.
evidence_page_or_section: Abstract; Sections 4-6, CUPS taxonomy, user study, and state-time analysis
verification_notes: Pilot B2 downgraded to B1. Although participants completed coding tasks, the measured effort construct is local interaction time with the recommendation system rather than end-to-end task completion.

title: Rocks Coding, Not Development: A Human-Centric, Experimental Evaluation of LLM-Supported SE Tasks
pilot_outcome: Coding task and typical software-development task
measured_outcome_verified: Time to complete the experimental task and solution quality for coding puzzles and a typical software-development bug-fixing task.
measurement_unit_verified: Task completion time in seconds; solution-quality score.
supporting_evidence: The typical development task required participants to fix two real bugs in a GitHub project. The paper states that fixing the issues requires modifying code and testing whether the issue is resolved. Task completion time is used as the efficiency/productivity measure.
evidence_page_or_section: Section 3, task design; Section 4, measures; Section 5.1.1, efficiency
verification_notes: Pilot B2 upgraded to B3 because testing is part of the measured participant workflow rather than only an offline correctness oracle.

title: Significant Productivity Gains through Programming with Large Language Models
pilot_outcome: Python programming tasks with Copilot, GPT-3, or browser baseline
measured_outcome_verified: Productivity while completing Python programming tasks under baseline, GitHub Copilot, and conversational GPT assistance.
measurement_unit_verified: Implemented requirements/features, task completion time, correctly implemented requirements, and characters per minute.
supporting_evidence: Participants performed three Python programming tasks. Efficiency is operationalized through the number of features or requirements implemented within the study timeframe and normalized task completion time. Correctness is assessed using predefined unit tests.
evidence_page_or_section: Sections 3.3-3.5; especially 3.4 Tasks and 3.5 Recorded Data
verification_notes: B2 retained. Predefined unit tests are an evaluation oracle for implemented features, not a participant testing/review workflow; therefore they do not justify B3.

title: Take It, Leave It, or Fix It: Measuring Productivity and Trust in Human-AI Collaboration
pilot_outcome: Programming exam; demonstrated performance and efficiency
measured_outcome_verified: Performance and efficiency on a programming exam completed with and without access to Bard.
measurement_unit_verified: Total exam score from 0 to 10 and total time spent on the exam.
supporting_evidence: The task-based study observes 76 software engineers completing a programming exam. Performance is the final exam score, while efficiency is defined as total time spent on the exam.
verification_notes: B2 retained because the objective productivity outcome ends at completion of the programming task/exam.

title: The Impact of AI-Pair Programmers on Code Quality and Developer Satisfaction: Evidence from TiMi studio
pilot_outcome: Code repositories and code reviews are analyzed, but the available evidence establishes code quality and developer satisfaction rather than a clearly bounded productivity/effort outcome.
measured_outcome_verified: Code quality and developer satisfaction in AI-pair and non-AI-pair projects.
measurement_unit_verified: Repository/code-review quality evidence plus survey/interview satisfaction evidence; no verified effort/time unit.
supporting_evidence: The primary abstract states that repository, code-review, survey, and interview data are used to measure and compare code quality and developer satisfaction. Time-saving is reported as a perceived benefit, not as a bounded productivity/effort outcome.
verification_notes: Presence of code-review data does not establish a B3 effort boundary. No concrete productivity/effort measure with an identifiable workflow boundary is supported by the accessible primary source.

title: The Role of Generative AI in Software Development Productivity: A Pilot Case Study
measured_outcome_verified: Practitioner experiences, uses, perceived benefits, challenges, and perceived individual productivity with generative AI.
measurement_unit_verified: Pilot case-study interviews/survey evidence.
supporting_evidence: The paper explicitly reports a generally positive perception of generative AI tools regarding individual productivity.
verification_notes: Productivity evidence is perceptual rather than a directly observed effort or work-output measure.

title: Trade-offs for Substituting a Human with an Agent in a Pair Programming Context: The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly
measured_outcome_verified: Programming productivity and code quality in human-human versus human-agent pair programming.
measurement_unit_verified: Task productivity, code-quality measures, self-efficacy, and qualitative interaction outcomes.
supporting_evidence: The study compares human-human and Wizard-of-Oz human-agent pairs and quantitatively evaluates productivity and code quality.
verification_notes: B2 because the measured productivity outcome concerns the pair-programming task rather than review, integration, or delivery.

title: Using an LLM to Help With Code Understanding
measured_outcome_verified: Task completion when developers use an IDE-integrated LLM for code understanding versus web search.
measurement_unit_verified: User-study task completion/performance and usage measures.
supporting_evidence: A user study with 32 participants finds that the contextualized LLM plugin can aid task completion more than web search.
verification_notes: B2 because the observed outcome is completion of the assigned code-understanding task.

title: What drives the corporate payoffs of using generative artificial intelligence?
measured_outcome_verified: Enterprise-level GenAI productivity gains across multiple business functions.
measurement_unit_verified: Throughput time, unit cost, task effectiveness, and related enterprise productivity measures.
supporting_evidence: The analysis combines GenAI use cases across content production, coding, customer acquisition, marketing/sales, and customer service.
verification_notes: Productivity is measured, but the software-development workflow boundary for the coding component cannot be identified from the reported aggregate measures.

title: An Empirical Study on How Large Language Models Impact Software Testing Learning
pilot_outcome: Software-testing learning task; tests written and effectiveness/efficiency outcomes
measured_outcome_verified: Effectiveness and efficiency while students learn and perform software-testing exercises using the Code Defenders environment.
measurement_unit_verified: Tests written, usefulness/effectiveness of tests, and related learning/performance measures.
supporting_evidence: Students practice testing concepts by writing tests and mutants in Code Defenders. The study reports concrete work-output measures, including number of tests and their usefulness.
verification_notes: B2 retained under Rule R5: writing tests is itself the focal implementation task. The study does not measure testing as a downstream verification stage of a previously implemented change.

title: “Will I be replaced?” Assessing ChatGPT's effect on software development and programmer perceptions of AI tools
measured_outcome_verified: ChatGPT code-generation effectiveness on LeetCode problems and programmer perceptions of AI tools.
measurement_unit_verified: Automated code-problem performance plus questionnaire responses.
supporting_evidence: Study 1 evaluates ChatGPT itself on 180 coding problems; Study 2 surveys 99 programmers about capabilities, trust, perceived productivity, and job-security concerns.
verification_notes: Model-only performance is not developer effort, while human productivity evidence is perceptual.

title: The role of firm AI capabilities in generative AI-pair coding
measured_outcome_verified: Firm-level productivity throughput and quality-adjusted productivity associated with generative-AI pair coding.
measurement_unit_verified: Reported firm-level productivity-throughput and quality-adjusted productivity measures; exact software-workflow operationalization not yet verified.
supporting_evidence: The study analyzes productivity implications of genAI pair coding across global firms and reports productivity throughput gains.
verification_notes: Productivity is clearly measured, but the accessible evidence is insufficient to determine whether throughput ends at local coding, completed implementation, or a broader workflow stage.

title: Don’t Complete It! Preventing Unhelpful Code Completion for Productive and Sustainable Neural Code Completion Systems
measured_outcome_verified: Performance of an early-rejection mechanism for low-value neural code-completion prompts.
measurement_unit_verified: Code-completion quality/acceptance prediction and computational efficiency measures.
supporting_evidence: The work proposes a mechanism to reject prompts likely to yield unhelpful code completions before invoking the large model.
verification_notes: No developer productivity/effort outcome with an identifiable workflow boundary is directly measured.

title: ChatGPT vs. Stack Overflow: An Exploratory Comparison of Programming Assistance Tools
pilot_outcome: Programming-assistance user tasks comparing ChatGPT and Stack Overflow
measured_outcome_verified: Code quality and task-completion speed for algorithmic, library-usage, and debugging programming tasks.
measurement_unit_verified: Code-quality scores and elapsed timestamps including first successful execution, first test case passed, submission, and time to fix individual bugs.
supporting_evidence: For algorithm tasks the study records first successful execution, first test case passed, and final submission. It also measures the interval used to modify/refine code until a test case passes. Debugging-task time is measured until individual bugs are fixed.
evidence_page_or_section: Section 3.1; Section 4.2 RQ2, Task Completion Speed; Tables 6-8
verification_notes: Pilot B2 upgraded to B3 because testing/debugging and code refinement are performed by participants and explicitly included in the measured task-completion timeline.

title: The impact of GitHub Copilot on developer productivity from a software engineering body of knowledge perspective
pilot_outcome: Industrial productivity measurement using throughput, cycle time, code quality, defects, and satisfaction; cycle time runs from in-progress to done, and defects are measured after production release.
measured_outcome_verified: Industrial productivity metrics: throughput, cycle time, code quality, defects, and developer satisfaction.
measurement_unit_verified: Story points/issues per sprint; work-item cycle time; code-quality measures; defects after release into production.
supporting_evidence: Cycle time is measured from in-progress to done, and defects are defined as issues or errors identified following release of code into production.
verification_notes: B4 retained because a measured productivity-related outcome extends beyond integration to defects observed after production release.

title: AI-Augmented Software Development: Boosting Efficiency and Quality
pilot_outcome: Paper discusses AI support across coding, testing, and deployment, but available evidence does not identify the measured productivity or effort boundary.
supporting_evidence: Accessible metadata and abstract-level material describe AI support across coding, testing, debugging, DevOps, and deployment, but do not establish a concrete measured productivity or effort outcome.
verification_notes: No boundary assigned. Mentions of testing/deployment do not establish that these stages are included in a measured productivity/effort outcome. Full text was not available from the accessible sources.

title: Can Generative AI Contribute to both productivity gains and human Flourishing, and in fine satisfaction at work? Research on GitHub Copilot use in Software Development
measured_outcome_verified: Self-reported productivity, flourishing, frustration, and job satisfaction among GitHub Copilot users.
measurement_unit_verified: Weekly and final questionnaire responses analyzed using CHAID/ANOVA.
supporting_evidence: Developers completed repeated surveys over ten weeks; productivity gain is one of the questionnaire constructs.
verification_notes: Productivity is self-reported and therefore does not provide an objective workflow-boundary measure.

title: Cautious Optimism: The Influence of Generative AI Tools in Software Development Projects
measured_outcome_verified: Developer perceptions, experiences, adaptations, benefits, and concerns regarding GenAI in software projects.
measurement_unit_verified: Qualitative evidence from industry professionals.
supporting_evidence: The study explicitly uses a qualitative methodology to capture sentiments and personal adaptive measures of professionals.
verification_notes: Reported workflow-efficiency benefits are qualitative perceptions, not directly measured effort.

title: ChatGPT as a Software Development Bot: A Project-Based Study
measured_outcome_verified: Student-reported effectiveness, benefits, limitations, learning, and proficiency when ChatGPT is used across SDLC phases.
measurement_unit_verified: Survey responses, descriptive statistics, and qualitative open coding.
supporting_evidence: Although student projects span requirements through deployment, the study's evaluation is based primarily on survey data concerning ChatGPT's impact and students' experiences.
verification_notes: Coverage of SDLC phases does not imply that effort through those phases was measured.

title: EveryBOTy Counts: Examining Human–Machine Teams in Open Source Software Development
measured_outcome_verified: Team productivity and work efficiency in human-only versus human-bot open-source software teams.
measurement_unit_verified: Pushes, issue comments, pull-request review comments, accepted/merged pull requests per team member, and issue-resolution time.
supporting_evidence: Productivity is operationalized using GitHub work events including accepted pull requests, while efficiency is measured through issue-resolution time. Accepted pull requests explicitly represent merged/integrated external code changes.
verification_notes: B4 because the productivity outcome explicitly includes merged pull requests, which cross the integration boundary.

title: The Evolution of Information Seeking in Software Development: Understanding the Role and Impact of AI Assistants
measured_outcome_verified: AI-assisted information-seeking behavior, perceived productivity, and skill development.
measurement_unit_verified: Mixed-method self-reported information-seeking evidence.
supporting_evidence: The study investigates information-seeking behavior and its impact on perceived productivity and learning rather than objective software-delivery effort.
verification_notes: Perceived productivity is outside the objective boundary-coding denominator.
